title: probabilistic-handoff-scorer-and-compact-telemetry-snapshot-format
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce probabilistic handoff scorer (opt-in) and a compact telemetry snapshot format (TSF) for faster on-call context loads; add handoff-eval CLI for simulating shift transitions; compatibility glue for incident-bot runbook suggestions; canary rollout and metrics to track triage latency and false-positive handoffs.
description:
Context and motivation: Oncall handoffs are a repeated source of cognitive load; responders often lack a compact, prioritized signal summarizing the last-decade (recent) activity and what changed during a shift. This PR adds two coordinated features: a probabilistic handoff scorer that ranks recent signals by likely relevance to the incoming responder, and a compact Telemetry Snapshot Format (TSF) to make handoff payloads small and fast to fetch.

High level changes and motivation: The scorer combines signal-level features (alert frequency, recent error rate deltas, SLO breach proximity, owner activity, recent playbook attachments) with a lightweight probabilistic model that outputs an ordered list of handoff candidates and a calibrated confidence score. TSF is a newline-delimited, gzip-friendly binary-compatible format that stores pre-aggregated counters, short traces and a tiny call-tree summary so the UI and incident-bot can present prioritized context in <150ms for typical accounts.

Commits (summary):
- initial: add scorer prototype and model weight schema (hand_off/scorer.py, hand_off/weights_v1.yaml)
- add: TSF serializer + deserializer (tsf/serializers.py, tsf/spec.md)
- add: CLI 'handoff-eval' and benchmark harness (cli/handoff-eval.py, benches/handshake_bench.py)
- tests: unit and integration tests for scorer and TSF (tests/test_scorer.py, tests/test_tsf_integration.py)
- docs: oncall handbook and rollout notes (docs/oncall/handoff.md)
- infra: helm values for feature flag and canary (charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml)

Changed areas (high level):
- slo_toolkit/hand_off/scorer.py  -- core algorithm, probability calibration and mode toggles
- slo_toolkit/tsf/serializers.py  -- TSF writer/reader and size heuristics
- cli/handoff-eval.py  -- local simulation tool for shift transitions and A/B comparisons
- docs/oncall/handoff.md  -- operator guide and emergency rollback instructions
- tests/*  -- new unit and integration tests to validate edge cases
- charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml  -- feature flag and canary rollout parameters

Backward compatibility and rollout: The scorer is behind a feature flag (slo.handoff.scorer.enabled) and TSF is opt-in for clients; incident-bot will negotiate TSF support during handshake. Default remains the existing JSON snapshot to avoid breaking older clients. Canary rollout plan included: 5% -> 25% -> 100% in three stages with automatic rollback on triage-latency regression >10% or increase in manual handoffs.

Performance and bench numbers: Microbenchmarks on staging telemetry (mixed prod traces sampled) show: median handoff snapshot deserialize time 18ms (vs 72ms with current JSON), end-to-end handoff load for UI reduced from 160ms to 48ms, and simulated triage time (closed-loop with handoff-eval) improved by ~3.6x for low-signal incidents where context fetch was previously dominant. Memory and CPU overhead are within acceptable limits: scorer inference ~0.6ms/request on a small worker; TSF serialization adds ~4KB per snapshot on median workloads.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Great direction. Two asks before approving: (1) show reproducibility steps for the weight schema and how weights are updated in prod, (2) add an explicit privacy doc: what PII could be included in TSF and how it's sanitized/encrypted."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added weights_v1.yaml and a small 'weights-repro' script in benches/ that deterministically replays the training seed; added TSF privacy section in docs/oncall/handoff.md and enforced PII scrub in tsf/serializers.py. PTAL."
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Please add unit test for empty-signal edge case and a test where owner metadata is missing — we had a flake in a similar PR previously." 
- Maya Chen: "Added tests/test_scorer.py::test_empty_and_missing_owner. Fixed a bug where missing owner caused NPE in the ranker; updated changelog." 
- Priya Nair (security reviewer): "Confirming encryption-at-rest for TSF when stored in object store and that the serializer doesn't leak raw traces. Let's add a runtime assertion in CI smoke that validates no trace payload >64KB escapes the TSF writer." 
- Maya Chen: "Added integration test to assert size and added S3 upload wrapper that sets SSE-KMS header when the feature flag is enabled. CI smoke added as a fast gating check."
- Liam O'Connor: "LGTM after CI passes; approving."

CI and gating: First CI run failed (unit test flake around missing-owner) — fixed in subsequent commit. Lint/format passed on second run; integration tests (synthetic telemetry) initially showed a size regression for a pathological trace; added a size-trimming heuristic to the serializer and re-ran integration tests. Final CI: all checks green (unit, integration, lint, bench smoke). ci_status: pass.

Security and safety checks: - TSF is opt-in; default snapshot unchanged. - PII scrub enforced with configurable scrub rules per-org. - Feature flag gating and canary rollout included; automated rollback hooks configured on SLO regressions.

Usage notes for operators: - To try locally: pip install -e . && python cli/handoff-eval.py --sample-size 100 --canary 0.05
- To enable for org: flip slo.handoff.scorer.enabled in chart values (see charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml). - On incident-bot side, add 'supports_tsf' to client capabilities; handshake code added in incident-bot compat layer (separate PR to incident-bot will reference this one).

Open questions and follow-ups: - Weights lifecycle: plan to introduce auto-tuning in a follow-up PR (ENG-8421). - Incident-bot integration PR to add TSF compatibility is tracked separately and will be canaried alongside this change.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals and all CI green. Canaries will run over the next 4 weeks as defined in rollout notes.
